title: The Empire Versus Civilization
author: Rob Urie
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/01/Screenshot-2026-01-28-at-5.58.55-PM-680x507.png)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

One aspect of the current clash of civilizations that goes largely unnoticed
in the US is that there is only one civilization, if we can call it that,
doing the clashing. That would be the US and its arrangement of vassals that
emerged from WWII. As if participating in an exploitation video called good
vassals gone bad, the former liberal governments of Europe have moved hard to
the foreign policy right. Through near-complete reversal of the Western
liberal order, the West is back to fighting WWII. Only without any defensive
missiles. Or competent leaders.

Rumors, as in stories in the mainstream press, have it that the US is running
dangerously low on defensive (‘interceptor’) missiles. Iran reportedly
possesses and has been using offensive (‘strike’) hypersonic missiles that fly
too fast to be reliably intercepted. The minimum lead time for the US to
produce more defensive missiles is three to five years. Without defensive
missiles, US ‘assets’ in the Gulf, including (US) military bases, cannot be
defended against Iranian missiles. That US military planners didn’t foresee
this suggests that competence isn’t their strength.

Not that Americans would know anything about it. No news or low-quality
propaganda are what we are fed. For one-and-one-half-trillion-dollars-per-year
(Pentagon budget), higher quality propaganda should be the least that we get.
Depending on the telling, either Ansar Allah (the Houthis) or Iran-affiliated
militias in Iraq (remember Iraq?) have destroyed critical oil and gas
infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Aramco Jizan and Abqaiq Oil
Stabilization Plant have been largely destroyed. Refineries and pipelines are
ablaze.

How oil prices declined as they did in the presence of major supply
disruptions tells us that markets have nothing to do with it. The US and its
allies have been depleting their SPRs (Strategic Petroleum Reserves) since the
launch of the US – Israeli war against Iran. The US SPR has about 300 million
barrels left out of a target level of 700 million barrels. The understanding
here is that the US military wants a minimum level of 350 million barrels. But
the Trump administration is willing to take it down to 70 million barrels.

An analogy would be spending your life savings to maintain the appearance of
prosperity going into a recession. If the economy recovers in time to restore
incomes, the strategy ‘works.’ But if it doesn’t, the cash cushion is gone and
the US goes from being rich to being poor the minute the savings run out. In
political space – time, if the SPR hasn’t been drained of oil by the midterm
elections, Donald Trump’s political chestnuts with respect to oil prices will
have been pulled out of the fire. That the day after election day the whole
charade could fall apart suggests that the US needs more robust systems of
political accountability.

But Donald Trump’s political fortunes are the least to be concerned with given
the events that have already transpired. The Saudi refineries that have been
destroyed represent critical infrastructure that feeds global oil and gas
supplies. Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG processing facility was significantly
destroyed in March. The Strait of Hormuz has now been substantially closed for
five months with no signs of reopening. And the world’s SPRs have been brought
to dangerously low levels. The time-to-repair for both the Saudi facilities
and Ras Laffan is five years. For those doing the math, the world is screwed.
The consequences of Trump’s war against Iran will be with us for decades.

Adding fuel to the fire is that Trump has scuttled the very possibility of
negotiations to end the conflict. Having bombed Iran twice in the midst of
negotiations and then treated the MOU as a joke, the Iranians are correct to
suspect that Trump is incapable of negotiating in good faith. Adding to the
evidence is the six months of US negotiations with Saudi Arabia regarding the
‘[123 agreement](https://mondoweiss.net/2026/07/the-farce-of-trumps-nuclear-
deal-with-saudi-arabia/)’ (details below) that Trump threw in the trash by
adding the condition that the Saudis sign on to the Abraham Accord
(recognizing Israel) _after_ both sides had signed the deal.

With respect to causes, upwards of forty million Iranians braved brutal summer
heat to attend the funeral of Iran’s martyred Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei.
This turnout would be the envy of any Western leader. It is evidence of a
relationship between the Iranian leader and the faithful that stands largely
outside of Western experience. His martyrdom is evidence of blindness by
Western leaders to the unifying effect of shared enemies. That US and Israeli
leaders had such a distorted view of how Ali Khamenei is viewed could and
should be revelatory. They don’t know what they are doing. The Israelis in
particular appear to be working from KKK training manuals.

The lies intended to frighten us into consenting to these wars–foreign threats
(e.g. WMD’s), insane or otherwise irrational foreign leaders, oppressed and
put upon people in desperate need of being ‘liberated,’ and resources that the
US wants, follow the same regime change script every time. We, the people, are
assumed to be well-trained monkeys who press a button and are fed the New York
Times’ non-explanation of events. And the paradox of psychological
manipulation is that we all have psychologies–even (especially) the
psychologists creating techniques of social control.

So, here we are. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed even though a guarantee
of global economic catastrophe is baked in to keeping it so. According to the
military commenters that I trust, there is no military solution that would end
Iran’s control over the Strait that wouldn’t also end humanity. The only
solution to the current quagmire is negotiation–which the US is incapable of.
In Trump-world, negotiation is for weaklings. This seems short sighted. Power
is in the process of being redistributed from West to East. As Bob Dylan put
it, ‘the loser today, will be later to win.’

So, how does this get resolved? Jeff Sachs’ solution is for both sides to just
stop fighting. As a near-term solution, Sachs’ logic is unassailable. The US
can’t be trusted to abide by an agreement, so why bother? The problem is that
neither Trump nor the Israeli leadership care if they light the world on fire.
The evidence? They are lighting it on fire. Pundits suggest that Trump and
Netanyahu are playing eight-dimensional-chess. Really? With apologies, aren’t
these the same people who attacked Iran without considering the Strait of
Hormuz? A drooling contest seems the better metaphor.

As much as I like the simplicity of the ‘just leave’ solution, this probably
has to be settled on the battlefield. While the take here is that the Iranians
prefer peace, the siege of Stalingrad–painful as it was, worked to the
advantage of the Soviets. Trump just tried rounds three and four of bombing to
open the Strait to no avail. Knowing that the US and Israel are out of
interceptor missiles, if I were Iran, I would make onerous demands to make up
for Trump’s fakery with respect to the MOU and then start leveling Tel Aviv as
I did so. The goal would be to make it so painful for the West to persist with
its attacks that it stops doing so.

As losers in this war of choice, both Trump and the Pentagon can still blow
things up. But as they do so, they are demonstrating their own impotence. The
point in blowing things up is to coerce a desired political outcome from one’s
adversary. But it was understood by March 2nd or 3rd that the US had committed
a major military blunder and that it would be lucky to exit the situation
intact. But rather than stop digging, Trump has doubled and tripled down.
Heads, he wins. Heads or Tails, the entire world loses. But hey, at least he
has his priorities straight?

If there exists a ‘fifth column’ in the US, it is Zionists. Donald Trump was
paid up to $250 million by Sheldon and Miriam Adelson to attack and murder
enemies of Israel. Amongst the current and former supporters of Trump of whom
I am aware, they all now see him as the agent of a hostile foreign power. Why
it is a surprise that the man who took the money then does the bidding of
Israel is itself a mystery. That this is politically acceptable to those
purporting to want to make America great again is one of the great mysteries
of the age.

Further, the US House of Representatives recently passed the NDAA (National
Defense Authorization Act) seeking to integrate parts of the US and Israeli
militaries. The apparent goal is to remove the multi-billion-dollar ($3.3
billion per annum) transfers of money to Israel that have created political
controversy in order to better hide the payments from the public. Question: if
the public favors the transfers, why hide them? And if the public doesn’t
favor the transfers, why make them?

While the NDAA hasn’t yet passed the Senate, rumor has it that the Senate
wants to fully integrate Mossad and the CIA. Given the reach that Israel
already has into US affairs and how despised it is by a large and growing
proportion of the American people, Zionist oligarchs appear intent on cramming
this integration down our throats. Mossad is less well regarded than Donald
Trump by much of the world. If the Congressional intent is to demonstrate that
the US really is a dystopian hellhole, it’s working.

This comes at a seemingly inopportune time for agents of Israel in the White
House and the US Congress. Israel created the failed plan that turned into
Trump’s plan of attack against Iran. It is amongst the worst– least
knowledgeable of the facts on the ground, most fantasy-filled regarding who it
is that is being attacked, plans ever conceived. The IDF and MOSSAD screwed
this up so badly that no rational nation would tie its fortunes to Israel.
This aligns with the [Alliance of
Democracies](https://allianceofdemocracies.org/) [declaring Israel to be the
least liked nation on the planet](https://146165116.fs1.hubspotusercontent-
eu1.net/hubfs/146165116/DPI%202026.pdf) in 2026.

Westerners typically see genocide as an intentional act (e.g., Gaza). But the
recklessness with which the US war against Iran is being prosecuted suggests
that the definition be expanded to cover acts so egregious that their very
recklessness confers legal liability. Donald Trump is reported to have
articulated the social emergency that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz
would create. ‘The world’ had only few weeks to get global energy supplies
moving again before mass starvation and economic calamity were guaranteed.
Well, those few weeks is up.

The economic destruction currently taking place is incalculable. Globalization
created interrelationships and dependencies that only work in one direction. A
global food system on which billions of humans depend, that itself depends on
petroleum-based fertilizers and the capacity to deliver food around the world,
is being destroyed. The global energy system that runs factories is being
destroyed. Millions to billions of human lives have been put at risk by people
who do not understand the consequences of their actions.

As the facts have it, the Strait of Hormuz was open and ship traffic flowed
until the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28th. This makes all of the
follow-on problems in the Strait the fault of the US and Israel. The American
practice of creating catastrophes and then pointing to them as the reason to
create more catastrophes is on full display. The US wants the Strait opened.
But it was open before the US and Israel attacked Iran. How socially
destructive these people are is awe-inspiring. It approximates the number of
stars in the universe.

The Iranians, likely in consultation with their allies, have recently foregone
direct attacks on Israel. The goal is most likely escalation management to
prevent a runaway conflict. But it also suggests that the Iranians perceive
the US to be controlling the war. Otherwise, turning Tel Aviv into Gaza would
seemingly be a priority. The logic is simple. If Israel is the problem, then
ending Israel would end the problem. Otherwise, chasing the US out of the
Persian Gulf–a stated Iranian objective- makes strategic sense.

Fans of schadenfreude had a good week as the US and Saudi Arabia signed the
‘123 agreement’ _facilitating_ the building of a nuclear reactor in Saudi
Arabia. The deal was reportedly negotiated and signed before Donald Trump
added the condition that the Saudis sign on to the Abraham Accord officially
recognizing Israel. This is akin to agreeing to buy a car before being told
that the motor needed to run it is a separate deal. The Saudis reportedly told
Trump where to stick his deal once the hidden condition was revealed.

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/statefair.png)

Image: Whereas forty million Iranians attended Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s
funeral. Trump’s National State Fair had difficulty drawing a few hundred
Americans. This bodes poorly for Western leaders hoping for a respectful send-
off. But keep heart. At least some of those who lost money on Trump’s crypto
grift will show up to see if they can get their money back. Were Trump and
Netanyahu to end their days in close proximity, the prospect of them spending
eternity together would beat those existentialist plays from the 1950s. If
there is a hell, that would be it.
_Source:_[_agriculture.com_](https://www.agriculture.com/partners-states-show-
their-stuff-the-great-american-state-fair-opens-in-d-c-12007242) _._

As far as the Saudis go, current events couldn’t be happening to a more
deserving group of people. A likely factor in Ansar Allah joining the fight is
to exact revenge for the Saudi genocide in Yemen. As with Israel in Gaza, the
US sold the Saudis the weapons with which to commit genocide and provided the
political cover to keep it quiet. The Saudis starved upwards of one million
Yeminis (UN says 377,000, but it always undercounts) as the US administration
at the time (2014 – 2015) looked on approvingly.

To the alleged Iranian nuclear threat, the ‘123 agreement’ should open some
eyes. The US couldn’t possibly object to nuclear proliferation given its
ongoing role in facilitating nuclear proliferation. Under Eisenhower’s ‘Atoms
for Peace’ program, the US gave Iran the only nuclear reactor that it was
known to possess until recently. This was when Iran was a US vassal. The
Iranian Revolution ended this vassalage in 1979. It is why the US is at war
with Iran. The US is a spurned imperial overlord. Think Misery in the Stephen
King novel by that name.

Israeli paranoia about Iran having nuclear weapons seems poorly considered.
Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei opposed the development of nuclear weapons
when he was martyred by the US and Israel. Skepticism by the Americans
regarding Iran’s intentions is understandable. Every word uttered by the US is
a lie. What the US does is called projection. The Americans assume that the
Iranians are lying because the Americans always, always, always lie. Recall
Trump telling us that the Iranian nuclear program had been ‘totally
obliterated’ in June 2025?

Now that Iran’s Supreme Leader has been martyred, some younger Iranians see
the North Korean model as the path forward. Recall the US’s relentless saber-
rattling against North Korea until it acquired and tested a nuclear weapon.
Guess what. The saber rattling has ended. The only mystery is why the
Americans still think this is a clever strategy? How many times does US
nuclear strategy need to blow up in our faces before ‘lessons are learned?’
For those unsure, the answer is once. But it quite conspicuously isn’t.

In ye olden days the US had an agreement with Iran called the JCPOA (Joint
Comprehensive Plan of Action) which precluded Iran from developing nuclear
weapons. It included a robust inspection regime and Iran was in full
compliance with the terms. Then Donald Trump tore the JCPOA up. His reasoning
was that he, the Donald, could negotiate a better deal. And then he attacked
Iran. Up to the point of the JCPOA being torn up, the Iranians claimed that
they didn’t want a nuclear weapon. Now that Iran has the US by the short and
curlies, US leverage isn’t what it used to be.

So, the Strait of Hormuz was open until the US and Israel attacked Iran on
February 28th. Now it is closed. And Iran was in full compliance with the
agreed upon protocol to limit nuclear proliferation until the US tore up the
deal. Give the Trump administration more time to ‘negotiate’ and Iran will be
charging us rent to live in our own houses. Negotiation requires having cards
to play (leverage). Otherwise, capitulation (surrender) is the alternative.

This points to a fundamental flaw in Trump’s ‘peace through strength’ mindset.
It makes it a tyrant’s creed. Capitulation to power isn’t peace. It is a state
of human bondage. Are orderly concentration camps where the people are docile
really the US vision of a great society? Isn’t this Israel’s vision for Gaza?
Counter to Nietzsche that Christianity is ‘the ultimate expression of slave
morality,’ Trump’s version is a _slaver_ morality. If compliance is noble
(‘peace’), why doesn’t the US comply with its international obligations?

Hopefully Americans aren’t so deluded as to imagine that getting rid of Trump
will solve this problem. Don’t get me wrong, please (peacefully) get rid of
Trump. The weather in Den Hague (The Hague) is very nice this time of year.
But the dysfunction infecting the US runs deep. Genocide Joe co-launched the
US – Israeli genocide in Gaza. And the establishments of both parties fully
support genocide in Gaza, ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, war against Iran,
war against Russia and a new Red Scare. The more that things change…

**Communism**

> “While Soviet communism was frequently driven by more practical great-power
> concerns – the preservation of the Soviet empire and the defense of its
> material interests around the globe – its Cuban successor was built around a
> near-singular obsession with the “liberation” of the Global South from its
> Western colonial oppressors.”
>
> – [US Department of State](https://www.state.gov/wp-
> content/uploads/2026/07/Cuba-Report.pdf).

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently commissioned a position paper (link
above) from the State Department trying to legitimate a coming US attack on
Cuba. The paper puts ideology forward as the motivating factor in both the
Cuban Revolution and in Cubans sending doctors abroad to where healthcare is
needed. As when Venezuela subsidized US heating fuel prices and the US shut
the program down, the Federal government doesn’t want Americans getting decent
healthcare. We might get used to it.

Otherwise, the Trump administration, the State Department, and the national
Democrats believe that they have a winning electoral strategy with a new Red
Scare. The obvious target of the US political establishment, Donald J. Trump
presiding, is recent electoral wins by the DSA (Democratic Socialists of
America). The source of the Red Scare rhetoric appears to be John Birch
Society pamphlets from the 1950s and 1960s. Stated differently, what is being
revived is crackpot rhetoric from cloistered ideologues, not historical
analysis.

The DSA seems an odd target. Its program is to run ‘socialists’ for public
office. The US has elected some solid socialists to public office like Kshama
Sawant. But the structural paradox of electing socialists to govern capitalist
political economy needs to be considered. There is no

argument here that self-styled socialists shouldn’t run for office and win.
The problem is that were every seat in the House, Senate and White House to be
occupied by socialists, Goldman Sachs, Northrup Grumman and Microsoft would
still run the country. As the saying goes, if voting changed anything, it
would be illegal.

This is in no way to be flippant. Electoral politics is one tactic amongst
many to employ. But the state of electoral politics in the US, with citizens
fleeing the state approved parties but no one to vote for outside of them, is
a major point of frustration for many. What is missing from consideration is
that the institutions of Western governance such as oligarch funded campaigns,
a Congress that runs on legal bribes, and corporate control over basic
government functions assure that nothing changes for the better, only for the
worse.

Part of what is inexplicable about the American system is that very few
Americans support the ‘political center.’ The framing as ‘center’ is
misstatement. The Danish NGO Alliance of Democracies [publishes a
survey](https://146165116.fs1.hubspotusercontent-
eu1.net/hubfs/146165116/DPI%202026.pdf) that asks the citizens of nations to
rank their own countries in terms of adherence to political principles like
democracy. In past years fewer than half of (American) respondents have
believed that the US is ‘a democracy.’ And the cause isn’t ideological. The
reasons given for the US not being a democracy are economic.

This difference in perceptions plays out with ‘authoritarian’ China ranked as
being much more democratic by the people of China than Americans rank the US
to be. In the AoD’s ‘objective’ democracy ranking, the US is ranked much
higher than China in ‘factual’ democracy. But the people aren’t buying it. The
reasons why the US isn’t considered to be democratic by Americans have to do
with corporate and oligarchic control over US politics. And this gets to the
DSA’s conundrum. Americans apparently prefer having control over their own
lives to pulling a lever every few years for someone who doesn’t represent our
interests.

In this light, Jacobin’s Bhaskar Sunkara was [recently
interviewed](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/16/opinion/democratic-socialist-
capitalism-bhaskar-sunkara.html) by the New York Times’ Ross Douthat. Sunkara
kept the conversation well inside the realm of electoral politics. In his
view, and Jacobin’s, socialism is an accumulation of socialists. Ownership of
the means of production was only mentioned in passing. The serial
disappointment that Americans feel watching progressives being absorbed into
the system has done little to shift political focus from personalities to
institutions.

Impressive is that very little attention was paid to the shift of the
political ‘center’ in the US from welfare-state liberalism to the fascist
right (a merging of corporate with state power, ethnic genocide in Gaza,
violent political repression by ICE and coming election fraud from the White
House). This is meant to be descriptively accurate, not insulting. To be
clear, this isn’t remorse over the direction of the country. It is to make the
point that no matter which party assumed power, every election in the last
five decades has moved the US farther to the political right.

That Democrats have also jumped on the Red Scare bandwagon confirms a lot of
premises. The Black Democrat Mayor of my immigrant filled city recently wrote
a missive that resembled boilerplate KKK propaganda from the 1950s. He
apparently doesn’t know that earlier versions of his views were used by Bull
Conner, Lester Maddox, George Wallace and various other segregationists to
slander Martin Luther King, Malcolm X and the entire Civil Rights movement.
But the ultimate paradox is that the mayor and Donald Trump have _exactly_ the
same views on the DSA. To portray the DSA as Bolsheviks is frankly moronic.
The Bolsheviks had a political program.

This American practice of explaining history through ideology works well as
propaganda because it ignores causes. For instance, Adolf Hitler rose to be
Chancellor of Germany in 1933, the worst year of the Great Depression in
Germany, while promising to right the German economy. The prominent historical
explanations of the rise of National Socialism include the punishing Treaty of
Versailles and the Great Depression. But to hear the Americans tell it,
Germans woke up one morning thinking that fascism was a great idea and then
brought Hitler to power.

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/Screenshot-2026-07-29-at-11.54.17-AM-680x451.png)

_Graph: Adolf Hitler rose to power in Germany in the very pit of the Great
Depression. The people of Germany were desperate. While the Weimar government
offered austerity cobbled together with more austerity, Hitler claimed to have
a way out of the Depression. In the early years, and largely through military
Keynesianism, the German economy recovered and then some. The Nazi folly was
overreach. This is the same problem that the US is currently experiencing.
Source:_[_wikipedia.com_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Nazi_Germany)
_._

A similar explanation of the Russian Revolution prevails. WWI began in 1915
and ended in 1918. The Russian Revolution was in 1917. Russia participated in
WWI and lost far more people than the Western powers did. This was against a
self-interested monarchy (Romanovs) that demonstrated utter contempt for the
lives of Russian troops in WWI as the Russian people starved. The idea that
the Bolsheviks were bored puffies playing hooky from their bond trading jobs
at Goldman Sachs to start a revolution is a low probability explanation. It is
easily countered with facts.

Likewise, the Cuban Revolution wasn’t a case of well employed and well-fed
people deciding that they were bored with the status quo and that a good cure
for this boredom would be to hold a revolution. As is always the case, the
people who rebelled saw little alternative to doing so. The American people
would have rebelled if they had been in Russia in 1917. The American
Revolution proves this. And the American people would have rebelled in Cuba in
1959 with this same evidence in hand. Revolutions are created by the existing
powers. They are an effect, not a cause.

Of course, the US State Department and the Trump administration are free to
contend that the American Revolution really was frivolous-- bored housewives
and lazy workers deciding that holding a Revolution was easier than doing the
dishes. if it cares to. Booting politically repressive and extractive colonial
overlords out of the country so that the people of the US could govern
themselves is the generic explanation given for the American Revolution. This
doesn’t seem frivolous to yours truly. In contrast to Donald Trump. Marco
Rubio and the US State Department, I support the American Revolution.

As the facts have it, Marco Rubio’s family left Cuba in 1956, three years
before the Cuban Revolution. Cuba at the time was run by the US-installed
strongman and [gangster friendly Fulgencio
Batista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Godfather_Part_II). The point:
neither Rubio nor his family ever lived in a communist nation. He has zero
personal experience with it. Everything that he knows about Cuba appears to
have come from the backs of cereal boxes. But there is a large and persistent
network of anti-communist activists tied to [US-sponsored terror
networks](https://www.nytimes.com/1986/01/09/opinion/l-terror-is-the-most-
effective-weapon-of-nicaragua-s-contras-938786.html) (and
[here](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/briefing-book/iran/2016-11-25/iran-contra-
affair-30-years-later-milestone-post-truth-politics)) [and the global
narcotics trade](https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB2/index.html).

Readers will recall that Donald Trump recently pardoned former Honduran
president Juan Orlando Hernández, who was convicted in 2024 of importing [400
**_tons_** of cocaine](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9qewln7912o) (and
[here](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/juan-orlando-hernandez-former-
president-honduras-sentenced-45-years-prison-conspiring)) into the US. In 2010
Honduras underwent a right-wing coup that [ousted the elected President Manuel
Zelaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Zelaya) and replaced him with a
State Department-approved caretaker government. Soon thereafter, ‘immigrant
armies’ of orphaned children from Honduras were being turned away at the US
border.

This reprisal of Red Scare politics comes at an interesting time. The original
Red Scare was largely a Western business grift. In 1953 the CIA and MI6
[created fake
‘communists’](https://archive.org/details/allshahsmenameri0000kinz_u6l8) in
order to explain why the US and Britain– ‘bastions of democracy’ both,
overthrew the elected government of Iran to seize Iran’s oil for themselves.
And when Jacobo Arbenz was ousted as President of Guatemala in 1954, consent
was manufactured in the US by claiming falsely that he was himself ‘a
communist.’ He wasn’t.

With the Soviet Union and the Chinese communists not exactly in hiding in the
1950s, were the narratives inside the US regarding ‘communism’ plausible,
these agencies wouldn’t have had to create fake communists in order to justify
US coups. In the early 1960s, with the US military claiming that the Soviets
had _tens of thousands_ of nuclear weapons capable of hitting the US, the
actual count was later revealed to be [four](https://therealnews.com/hitler-
wouldnt-risk-doomsday-but-the-united-states-did-daniel-ellsberg-on-rai-2-8)
(part of 13-part series). The motivation for the US military to lie about the
matter is that the service budgets were based on perceived threats.

In terms of raw totalitarian excess, it was the CIA’s MKULTRA program that
produced the Unabomber, Ted Kaszynski, who killed three and injured 23 with
mail bombs. After having his personality ‘broken down and then pieced back
together’ by the CIA, brilliant mathematician and reported volunteer for the
MKULTRA program Kaszynski went full terrorist. This was initially posed as
‘left-wing’ violence and Kaczynski’s manifesto was put forward to support the
charge. It wasn’t until the forced disclosure of the CIA’s MKULTRA program
that the CIA’s involvement was revealed.

American slavery remains relevant in 2026 because while it was underway it was
a capitalist institution. Human beings, called slaves, were bought and sold as
‘capital’ just like a tractor, a loom or automation AI. So, one can criticize
slavery in moral terms. But the fact that some people (the owners of slaves)
made very good livings from the labor of others (slaves) set the terms for US
labor relations through to DOGE. This isn’t ideology speaking. It is history.
If someone wants to seriously claim that slaves weren’t considered capital,
please have at it.

So, American slavery nominally ended with the Civil War in 1865. But the
management practices developed on slave plantations in the American South
[form the basis of corporate Human Resources
departments](https://hbr.org/podcast/2018/11/why-management-history-needs-to-
reckon-with-slavery) (and [here](https://www.library.hbs.edu/working-
knowledge/the-messy-link-between-slave-owners-and-modern-management)) today,
right now. This is to draw a line directly from the slavery practiced in the
US up through 1865 to the rejection letter that you didn’t receive for that
job that you applied for because US corporations don’t ‘do’ respect for your
humanity because you are a commodity to them, ‘labor.’

One of the political challenges of my own youth was the Vietnam War. It was
explained at the time as a fight to the death between freedom and communism.
In fact, Vietnam was a former French colony that the US assumed control of
from France following WWII. The US created internal divisions in Vietnam and
then posed the resulting civil war as ‘communist aggression.’ But it wasn’t
communist aggression. [It was a civil
war](https://www.errolmorris.com/film/fow_transcript.html). Once the US left
